---
title: "Tutorial: small-molecule binding site identification"
---

This tutorial identifies binding pockets in the biotin-binding protein streptavidin
([PDB 1STP](https://www.rcsb.org/structure/1STP)).

**You will learn to:**

- run AutoSite on a macromolecule
- find and understand the output files AutoSite generates

**Prerequisites:** ADFRsuite 1.0 [installed](download.qmd) with `ADFRsuite-1.0/bin` on your
`PATH`, and the [tutorial data](https://ccsb.scripps.edu/autosite/wp-content/uploads/sites/50/2021/10/1STP.tgz)
downloaded.

## 1. Run AutoSite

AutoSite needs the macromolecule in PDBQT format. Unpack the input file `1STP.pdbqt`:

```bash
tar zxvf 1STP.tgz
```

Run AutoSite on it:

```bash
autosite -r 1STP.pdbqt
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

radius of gyration, energy per volume, buriedness, score, and its feature points by type.

## 2. Output files

The output files are written in the folder where AutoSite runs.

- `1STP_AutoSiteSummary.log`: the log, with the output printed to the terminal.
- A folder `1STP/` containing:
    - the cluster points, one PDB file per cluster (`1STP._CL.xxx.pdb`)
    - the feature points, one PDB file per cluster (`1STP_fp_xxx.pdb`)
    - a CSV file with the cluster scoring function values for each cluster (`1STP_summary.csv`)
    - the AutoGrid input file used to compute the grids (`rigidReceptor.gpf`)
    - the AutoGrid output files (`rigidReceptor.glg`, `rigidReceptor.x.map`)

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Review note
- The cluster file pattern is written `1STP._CL.xxx.pdb` on the CCSB page, unlike the feature
  point pattern `1STP_fp_xxx.pdb`. Check the real file names.
- The CCSB page wrote the CSV file as `91STP_summary.csv` (a typo for "(1STP_summary.csv"); fixed.
- The console output points to `http://adfr.scripps.edu/AutoDockFR/autosite.html`, which no
  longer responds. Kept as printed by the program.
- The CCSB page does not explain the feature-point columns (D, A, Other) of the table.
:::
